reason: Holds. Read the archive.org text of the New Directions A Season in Hell and The Drunken Boat (Varèse; copyright 1945, 1952, 1961; NDP97 1961). Under FAREWELL, the paragraph beginning 'Meanwhile this is the vigil' reads, word for word and comma for comma: 'And, in the dawn, armed with an ardent patience, we shall enter magnificent cities.' One paragraph follows ('Why talk of a friendly hand!'), then April-August 1873, so second to last is correct. Attribution is Rimbaud's own voice, not a character. The line is famous in its own right (Neruda built his 1971 Nobel lecture on it) and it is hopeful. shipped.js: clean, Rimbaud 0 of 3, not banned. The source line is 102 characters with no dash. A prose poem tagged Poetry is acceptable. Minor note: the 1961 date is the revised Varèse text; the 1945 first version may differ, so keep 1961.
